# Architecture planning

## Trigger

Use this Skill to produce and iterate an evidence-based working plan for a feature, refactor, or customization workflow before edits.

## Inputs

- Approved requirements, the inspected Research document or agreed issue-bearing Review report, and relevant repository evidence.
- For a Review-origin plan, its direct implementation-report, previous-plan, and original-Research lineage.

## Procedure

Use this skill to produce and iterate an evidence-based working plan without independently changing repository files. Investigate and disclose uncertainty; an agent readiness opinion does not veto an engineer-approved, inspected-version transition. Plan defines the outcome, acceptance and material boundaries; Implement chooses ordinary in-boundary details.

### Delegated analyst boundary

When this skill is applied by a delegated analyst, perform only the applicable evidence-gathering and analysis steps below, then return a narrow planning-lens report. The report may identify requirements, affected locations, reusable patterns, options, trade-offs, risks, validation considerations, and unanswered questions with citations. It is non-persistent input to the Plan coordinator: do not complete a plan template, author or alter Work Item, Task, or Step hierarchy, allocate, select, create, persist, revise, or authorize lifecycle artifacts, handoffs, commands, cleanup, scope, hierarchy, or approvals. Only the Plan coordinator may synthesize, author, and persist the canonical implementation plan.

1. Read the inspected Research document or agreed issue-bearing Review report and its direct implementation-report, previous-plan and original-Research lineage; inspect the affected repository areas.
2. Map each requirement to affected files, symbols, interfaces, or documentation sections.
3. Identify existing patterns to reuse and alternatives that should be rejected.
	Reconcile every architectural choice from Research and every planning discovery using the [ADR capability](../architecture-decision-records/SKILL.md). For each choice retain rationale, realistic alternatives and option-specific reasons, actual selection or explicit pending state, conditions and affected Work Item IDs. Bind inspected coverage by actual ADR path/ID, identifiable section, substantive version/snapshot, state and actual agreement evidence/conditions. Inspect existing records for substantive applicability before reuse; do not duplicate verified appropriate coverage. Group choices only where shared context, rationale and governance are clear, preserving each choice individually rather than hiding omissions in an umbrella record. Independently changing status, authority or supersession favours separate records. Proportionality governs detail, not coverage, even for small reversible spikes; one correct bound ADR does not establish completeness. If no architectural choices are identified, give an evidence-supported routine-only disposition. Delegated analysts supply findings only; the coordinator owns reconciliation in the canonical Plan and any authorized Proposed draft.

	Topology, technology/toolchain baselines, public contracts and security/data boundaries are architectural signals. Dependency/test-framework changes require context about platform, integration, compatibility and operating commitments. Naming, helper extraction and architecture-preserving repairs remain routine Implement-owned choices without ADR reference. Resolve material classification ambiguity with the engineer using evidence through the question-resolution method; analysts return the ambiguity to the coordinator. Unknown destinations, unavailable records, pending decisions/agreement or unmet decision-critical conditions need explicit gaps, dependent effects and resolution routes, not invented coverage, Accepted state or governance requirements. These constrain dependent effects, not phase invocation or independent safe work. Only the Plan coordinator retains the narrowly guarded associated Proposed-ADR exception; preserve accepted/superseded history, actual agreement and separate directory/file guards.
4. Define the delivery approach, including sequencing or rollout only when applicable, dependencies, controls, and key mitigations.
5. Inspect relevant build, test and script surfaces before finalizing validation. Specify the outcome, material constraints and useful checks without predicting every debugging invocation. Do not invent commands, evidence, paths, frameworks or dependencies.
6. Complete the [implementation plan template](./implementation-plan-template.md) with the inspected predecessor, one authoritative Work Item register and matching, numbered Work Item → Task → Step detail as the normal proportionate hierarchy. Map each item to Research/requirements evidence and observable acceptance, with relevant checks and dependencies where applicable; define an explicit Work Item exit gate tying that acceptance to every required validation and its specified successful result. Meaningful units govern detail, not an exhaustive task/command list or minimum item count. Start completion markers unchecked; they track execution progress only and are not standalone proof of validation, approval or Review acceptance. Implement persists existing Step and Task markers as outcomes complete and checks a Work Item only after its explicit gate passes; see the [incremental progress method](../safe-implementation/SKILL.md). Plan owns scope, hierarchy and acceptance; Implement selects ordinary in-boundary details. An engineer-approved material Review finding may warrant a new Plan; a supported original-criteria correction instead returns manually to Implement under the original approved Plan. Do not rewrite historical evidence or invent unresolved choices.
7. Identify relevant checks and their expected effects, including reconciliation of every architectural choice against inspected ADR coverage and explicit dependent gaps. Implement may run permitted local checks directly or use Script Runner as an optional specialist; Research and Review remain source-read-only. Plan remains source/configuration-read-only except for the lifecycle core's narrowly guarded creation/revision of a directly associated Proposed ADR during active planning. Use the [architecture decision records Skill](../architecture-decision-records/SKILL.md) for coverage and authority safeguards. Real platform denial and uncertain destructive or external completion still require reconciliation.
8. Direct the owning Plan coordinator to persist and read back a contained, numbered physical working Plan in the verified Research folder before claiming canonical Plan output. A non-local draft or locator is not a substitute; if the save or readback fails, disclose unfinished output while continuing safe planning work. Keep current questions and evidence limits explicit. Freeze the inspected physical version when later supplied to `/implement`; persistence alone never authorizes edits.

### Resolve material planning gaps

Investigate material planning gaps and disclose what remains unresolved. Use [agent-question-resolution](../agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md) to route factual questions and obtain engineer decisions on material scope or policy choices. Continue the Plan document while answers or evidence are pending; an unresolved question does not veto an engineer-approved transition for the inspected version. An effect that depends on unresolved scope or authority remains ineligible until its own guard is satisfied.

1. Inspect the request, the inspected predecessor and relevant repository evidence before treating anything as a gap. Record each material gap with its supporting facts, inferences and remaining unknowns.
2. For every material gap, record an evidence-supported answer when one is available; otherwise record the remaining question and its dependent effect. Do not invent a target, design, rule, dependency, validation condition or operator choice.
3. For factual gaps, investigate directly or use a suitable read-only specialist when useful. Specialists report facts and recommendations; they do not decide operator-owned choices or authorize work.
4. For operator-owned choices, or material questions still unresolved after evidence inspection and suitable specialist investigation, use [agent-question-resolution](../agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md) to explain what is known, what remains unknown and which decision or dependent effect cannot proceed, then ask the engineer directly one decision at a time. Do not delegate an operator-owned decision.
5. Revise the plan when an answer changes its material scope or acceptance. Continue planning while investigating; record unresolved questions and evidence limits accurately. A clarification answer resumes planning and is not approval of a transition.

The plan may retain unresolved questions and incomplete evidence. The engineer's `/implement` invocation with the inspected Plan transfers ownership of the bounded outcome even if an agent advised further planning. Identify effects dependent on unresolved **material** decisions; ask the engineer before changing those commitments. Ordinary implementation investigation, related-file/test selection and attributable repair need no predicted branch or new approval. Continue independent work and report evidence limits honestly.

Specify the approved outcome, material boundaries and acceptance without requiring prediction of every local repair, test or related file. Implement chooses ordinary in-boundary details and preserves original criteria. Every prospective Plan must state one explicit bounded local staging/append-only commit strategy: repository/worktree/branch selection rule, approved content and exclusions, Script Runner ownership, candidate-relevant validation, local-policy constraints, validity and revocation. Every detailed Work Item must include a commit-plan entry referencing that strategy, its normal post-validation checkpoint boundary and coherent content/purpose, or a specific justified combination, deferral or no-commit exception. Use existing IDs, not a second register or repeated Git procedures. Each exception states the actual constraint/reason, affected IDs, validation/dependency consequence, later boundary if one exists and why the normal boundary is unsuitable. Supported engineer constraints, effective local policy or inseparable dependencies can justify departures; unknown future obstacles cannot be invented. Empty headings, generic exemptions and unexplained blanket prohibitions fail planning assessment. An actual prohibition still supplies no Git authority, including in historical Plans; do not rewrite them to adopt this prospective default.

Approval of that inspected Plan includes only its covered commits after `/implement`, without a separate grant exchange; a candidate need not exist at approval. Silent, prohibited or unapproved-option Plans do not authorize Git, and Plan publication cannot authorize its own checkpoint or earlier Research effects. Normal cadence is a checkpoint after each completed eligible coherent validated Work Item before unrelated work, with proactive consideration of earlier coherent validated Task boundaries in larger items. Avoid arbitrary thresholds, artificial splitting or commit gates. Implement accounts for each expected boundary against the Plan with actual disposition evidence before unrelated work; runtime obstacles are fresh implementation evidence, not retrospective substantive Plan exceptions. Use the shared [local Git checkpoint capability](../local-git-checkpoints/SKILL.md) for runtime candidate, helper, preservation and permission checks and the separate phase-record grant route. Missing material scope, new dependency or changed security/compatibility commitment requires an engineer decision; publication alone does not authorize source edits.

## Limits

For a material Review-origin plan, record the inspected source Review/version, reviewed implementation report/version, prior Plan/version and original Research/version. Use direct same-folder links only for real numbered records; otherwise retain the actual locator and inspected version. Do not require a new Plan for supported corrections to the original criteria: the engineer can resume Implement with the original approved Plan and linked Review context for fresh implementation evidence and independent re-review. Preserve mixed/unclear findings without guessing fixes. A verified clean Review records acceptance; optional status bookkeeping does not create it.

## Validation

Check that the plan's outcome, boundaries, acceptance and relevant validation are evidence-based and feasible. Describe consequential command/external effects when known, without requiring a command inventory for ordinary debugging. Implement may execute permitted local checks directly or consult Script Runner; neither route overrides platform denial. Reconcile uncertain destructive or external effects before repeating them. Record saves still require actual containment, permission, non-overwrite and readback under the lifecycle core. Mark material unresolved decisions explicitly; do not invent dependencies, commands or facts. Plan persistence does not authorize implementation.

## Outputs

- A narrow, cited planning-lens report for a delegated analyst; it is non-persistent input to the Plan coordinator.
- A contained, numbered physical working implementation plan saved and read back only by the Plan coordinator, with its unresolved questions and evidence limits explicit; otherwise an honestly unfinished draft.
